newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mayors from Canada, Mexico, U.S to confer on trade.
newsitem.headline: Mayors from Canada, Mexico, U.S to confer on trade.

text.p: Mayors from Canada, Mexico and the United States will begin meeting on Wednesday outside the northern Mexican city of Monterrey at a conference intended to strengthen North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) trade ties, organizers said on Tuesday.
Participants at the so-called First Summit of Mayors plan to sign an unspecified cooperative agreement, according to a statement.
Mayors sponsoring the event are from Kansas City, Missouri; Winnipeg, Manitoba; Dallas, Texas; Guadalajara, Jalisco; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma; and San Nicolas de los Garza, Nuevo Leon.

Organizer Ulises de la Garza told Reuters that 83 mayors had confirmed their assistance. A total of more than 250 people had confirmed they would attend, including local government and chamber of commerce representatives.
The conference will focus on increased technology and infrastructure investments, trade and economic development initiatives and cooperative trade marketing strategies, the statement said.
Participants aim to set up a commission to coordinate efforts to reach the goals of the conference, organizers said.
Other cities whose representatives that have confirmed attendance include: Witchita, Kansas; Des Moines, Iowa; Calgary, Alberta; Monterrey, Nuevo Leon; Saltillo, Coahuila; and Laredo, Tamaulipas.
